title: quartodown
text:
quartodown is an R package that turns your package’s README, help pages and vignettes into a website, rendered entirely by Quarto.


pkgdown can render Quarto vignettes, but it replaces Quarto’s styling with its own (theme: "none", minimal: TRUE). As a result, Quarto features such as callout blocks, code annotations and tabsets don’t render correctly; callouts, for instance, become plain blockquotes.
quartodown renders the whole site with Quarto itself, so you get:

full Quarto support, on every page;
a package website layout: a home page sidebar, a grouped function reference, articles and a changelog;
function links with hover tooltips.




Install from GitHub:
pak::pak("https://github.com/BjarkeHautop/quartodown")



Browse around to see how it looks! If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown.yml, with a reference: field that lists your package’s current functions in one section; edit it to group them however you’d like, in the same shape as pkgdown’s reference: field. It also gitignores the files the build generates.
Then build the site:
quartodown::build_site()
A preview can then be viewed using quartodown::preview_site().
The navbar is built from your vignettes: the one named after the package (or the only top-level one) becomes “Get started”, and the rest, including those in vignettes/articles/, go under “Articles”. See ?quartodown::build_site for everything quartodown.yml can configure.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Details
An existing _quartodown.yml is never overwritten.
use_quartodown() adds the following lines to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore (only the ones not already present in each file):

# .gitignore
_quarto/*
!_quarto/_freeze/

# .Rbuildignore
^docs$
^_quarto$
^_quartodown\.yml$


_quarto/ is the Quarto project build_site() generates and renders into docs/. Its _freeze/ directory holds the results of code run with build_site(freeze = TRUE), which can be committed so later builds, e.g. on CI, reuse them.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to _quartodown.yml.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Examples

pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_quartodown(pkg)
#> Wrote '/tmp/RtmpIlyxli/examplepkg19525bb3b0f8/_quartodown.yml' (edit this to group your functions).
#> Added '_quarto/*', '!_quarto/_freeze/' to '/tmp/RtmpIlyxli/examplepkg19525bb3b0f8/.gitignore'.
#> Added '^docs$', '^_quarto$', '^_quartodown\.yml$' to '/tmp/RtmpIlyxli/examplepkg19525bb3b0f8/.Rbuildignore'.
#> 
#> Next steps:
#>   1. Edit _quartodown.yml to group your functions the way you want.
#>   2. Run: quartodown::build_site()
#>   3. Preview site: quartodown::preview_site()
readLines(file.path(pkg, "_quartodown.yml"))
#>  [1] "# Configuration for quartodown::build_site(). See ?quartodown::build_site for"
#>  [2] "# all fields, including `articles:` (navbar order) and `quarto:` (extra"      
#>  [3] "# Quarto settings)."                                                          
#>  [4] ""                                                                             
#>  [5] "# Groups the function reference index, in the same shape as pkgdown's"        
#>  [6] "# `reference:` field."                                                        
#>  [7] "reference:"                                                                   
#>  [8] "  - title: All functions"                                                     
#>  [9] "    contents:"                                                                
#> [10] "      []"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

title: Get started with quartodown
text: quartodown builds a website for an R package with Quarto. This guide sets up a package, builds its site, and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Set up
From the root of your package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown.yml at the package root, the one configuration file you edit, and adds the files the build generates to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore. The configuration file is optional: without it, the site is built with the defaults.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Build the site
quartodown::build_site()
quartodown::preview_site()
build_site() builds the site into docs/, and preview_site() opens it in your browser.






Tip



Examples in the man pages and code in the vignettes run against your package’s current source: build_site() installs it into a temporary library first. To skip the install while iterating, use build_site(devel = TRUE), which loads it with pkgload::load_all() instead.


The site is built from what’s already in your package:

Home page: README.md, with a sidebar of links, the license, citation and developers taken from DESCRIPTION. Badges between <!-- badges: start --> and <!-- badges: end --> move into the sidebar.
Reference: one page per man/*.Rd file, and an index of them.
Get started: the vignette named after the package, like this one.
Articles: every other vignette, including those in vignettes/articles/.
Changelog: NEWS.md, with issues (#123) and GitHub users (@user) linked.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Organize the reference index
By default the reference index lists every function in one section. To group them, edit the reference: field in _quartodown.yml. It has the same shape as pkgdown’s:
reference:
  - title: Setting up
    contents:
      - use_quartodown
  - title: Building
    contents:
      - starts_with("build_")
?build_site lists the other fields: articles: sets the order of the “Articles” menu, and quarto: changes the Quarto configuration, e.g. to add navbar links.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Publish on GitHub Pages
This GitHub Actions workflow builds the site and deploys it to the gh-pages branch on every push. Save it as .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

name: quartodown

jobs:
  quartodown:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: quartodown-${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.run_id }}
    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: any::knitr, any::rmarkdown, github::BjarkeHautop/quartodown, local::.
          needs: website

      - name: Build site
        run: quartodown::build_site()
        shell: Rscript {0}

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4
        with:
          clean: false
          branch: gh-pages
          folder: docs
local::. installs your package’s dependencies, which its examples and vignettes need. Then, on GitHub, set the repository to serve Pages from the gh-pages branch (Settings → Pages).

title: Technical details
text: quartodown builds the site in three stages: it generates a Quarto website project from the package sources, renders it with Quarto, and adds hover tooltips to the result. The man pages, vignettes and the generated pages around them are all Quarto pages, so every Quarto feature works.

title: Technical details
text:
How a build works
quartodown::build_site() runs in three stages:

Before rendering, it writes a Quarto project into _quarto/: a reference page per man page, the vignettes, the changelog, license and community files, and the generated pages and theme files below.
During rendering, Quarto renders _quarto/ into docs/, running the examples and vignette code. Quarto runs each page’s code in a new R process, which loads the package from the library, so build_site() first installs the package into a temporary library and puts it first on that process’s library path. With build_site(devel = TRUE), it skips the install and has each process load the package from source with pkgload::load_all().
After rendering, it adds hover tooltips to the HTML in docs/.

The only file you edit is _quartodown.yml. Everything in _quarto/ is rewritten on every build, and gitignored by quartodown::use_quartodown():
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                      # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, with issues and users linked
├── quartodown.scss               # theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── quartodown-header.html        # dark-mode default
└── quartodown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
As in pkgdown, the reference pages are served at reference/<topic>.html, and docs/pkgdown.yml tells other sites’ downlit links where to find them.

title: Technical details
text:
Before rendering

The home page
index.md holds the README next to a sidebar with links, the license, the citation, the developers and the README’s badges. On narrow screens the sidebar moves below the content.
A README <picture> with a light and a dark version (GitHub’s prefers-color-scheme convention) becomes one <img> per theme, switched by the site’s light/dark toggle.


The reference index
To group and order the function index, _quartodown.yml has a reference: field in the same shape as pkgdown’s:
reference:
1  - title: Building the site
2    desc: >
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
3      - use_quartodown
4      - starts_with("build_")

1

Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.

2

An optional description, shown under the heading.

3

A topic, by any of its \alias{} names.

4

A selector, as in pkgdown: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains(), matches(), has_concept(), has_keyword(), - to exclude and c() to combine.




The navbar and footer
The navbar links the “Get started” vignette, the reference index, the other vignettes under “Articles” and the changelog. The footer has a “Developed by …” line, built from Authors@R.






TipChanging the Quarto configuration



A quarto: field in quartodown.yml is merged over the generated configuration. Lists, like the navbar’s items, are appended to; any other setting is replaced, and ~ removes it. For example, to add a navbar link and fold code blocks:
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true

title: Technical details
text:
The man pages
Each man/*.Rd file, except \keyword{internal} ones, becomes _quarto/reference/<name>.qmd. It’s rendered to HTML with tools::Rd2HTML(), as R’s help does, and then adjusted for the site:

Rd macros work: the package’s own (RdMacros: in DESCRIPTION, or man/macros/), such as Rdpack’s \insertRef{}, and build-time \Sexpr{}s such as \doi{}.
Usage, and code blocks with a language, such as roxygen’s ```yaml, are syntax-highlighted with a copy button.
Inline code is rendered as Markdown code spans, so quotes and backslashes survive Pandoc, and \eqn{}/\deqn{} render as math.
Examples run, with their output in the same block, prefixed with #>. \dontrun{} code is shown but not run, \dontshow{} code is run but not shown, and @examplesIf examples run only if their condition holds. A page whose examples all are in \dontrun{} renders without starting an R session.

title: Technical details
text:
After rendering: hover tooltips
After rendering, build_site() links every reference to one of the package’s functions, in code blocks or inline code, to its man page. Hovering shows a tooltip with its usage and the first sentence of its description. Try it: hover over build_site() or use_quartodown().
The sentence is cut off at 200 characters, and build_site() warns when one is longer. To build without tooltips, use build_site(tooltips = FALSE).

title: Technical details
text:
The theme
quartodown.scss, written for Quarto’s HTML (and originally adapted from pkgdown’s stylesheet), is layered on top of Quarto’s own themes:
theme:
  light: [default, quartodown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, quartodown.scss]
darkly normally uses the Lato web font and larger headings, so text would reflow when toggling between light and dark. quartodown.scss therefore sets Bootstrap’s system font stack and heading sizes for both themes.
Two things need JavaScript:

Dark mode by default. quartodown-header.html starts new visitors on the dark theme if their system prefers it.
Aligning the navbar title with the body text. The body’s left edge differs between the home page and other pages, so quartodown-after-body.html measures it and adjusts the navbar’s padding.

Usage

title: Build the package website
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the package root.




tooltips


Logical. Link references to the package’s own functions (in code blocks and inline code) to their reference page, with a hover tooltip showing the function’s usage and the first sentence of its description?




freeze


Logical. Reuse the results of code that ran in an earlier build, for pages whose source hasn’t changed since? Uses Quarto’s freeze, which keeps them in _quarto/_freeze/.




quiet


Logical. Hide Quarto’s rendering output?




devel


Logical. By default, the examples and vignettes run against the package installed from path into a temporary library. With devel = TRUE, they run against it loaded with pkgload::load_all() instead, which is faster, but code that starts other R processes (e.g. with callr or parallel workers) won’t find the package there.

title: Build the package website
Build the package website
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to the built site.

title: Build the package website
text:
Configuration
_quartodown.yml, at the package root, is optional; use_quartodown() creates one. It can contain:


reference: groups the function reference index, in the same shape as pkgdown’s reference: field. contents entries can be a topic alias or a selector: starts_with(), ends_with(), contains(), matches(), has_concept(), has_keyword(), - to exclude, and c() to combine. Without it, every topic is listed in one section.


articles: the order of the "Articles" navbar menu, as vignette paths relative to vignettes/ without extension (e.g. articles/details). Without it, every vignette other than the "Get started" one is listed, top-level vignettes first, then those in vignettes/articles/.


quarto: settings merged over the generated Quarto configuration. Settings are merged key by key: a list of entries (e.g. the navbar’s left: or right: items) is added to, any other value is replaced, and ~ removes a setting. For example, to add a navbar link:
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com


The "Get started" link points to the vignette named after the package, or to the only top-level vignette if there is just one.
